question: Should approval-bound `system.run` support an opt-in configuration that permits symlinked cwd paths after retaining canonical-target display and inode revalidation?
rationale: This is a deliberate weakening of a shipped TOCTOU hardening rule and introduces a new persistent configuration surface; the code review cannot determine the repository’s acceptable residual threat model.

options.title: Approve a narrow opt-in
options.body: Accept the setting after a security owner confirms the retained canonical-path and identity checks are sufficient, the documentation path is fixed, and real OpenClaw proof is supplied.

options.title: Keep canonical cwd mandatory
options.body: Reject the relaxation and instead improve the denial message and documented canonical-cwd remediation path.

options.title: Design a narrower capability
options.body: Request an owner-designed alternative that preserves the existing default and scopes any trusted-path exception more narrowly than a global boolean.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow opt-in
recommendation.body: Accept the setting after a security owner confirms the retained canonical-path and identity checks are sufficient, the documentation path is fixed, and real OpenClaw proof is supplied.

likelyOwner.reason: The available issue evidence ties tdjackey to the original hardening rationale, so they are the strongest available low-confidence routing candidate for this threat-model decision.
